newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament to debate tax shortfall Friday.
newsitem.headline: German parliament to debate tax shortfall Friday.

text.p: Germany's political parties will debate the latest estimate of 1997 tax receipts in a special parliamentary session on Friday, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) said on Thursday.

Joachim Hoerster, whip for the parliamentary group of the CDU and their sister party the Bavarian Christian Social Union, said the main opposition Social Democrats (SPD) had accepted the ruling coalition's invitation to debate the tax estimate.

Government and private tax experts have estimated that tax revenues in 1997 would be 18 billion marks less than previously forecast. Of the total, federal tax revenues would be 9.1 billion marks below budget, raising the spectre of a higher budget deficit.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel told a press conference that he would prepare proposals on how to plug the gap in financing in discussion with government coalition parties and the SPD, but declined to give any details.
He said he would step up privatisations and would not rule out tax increases.
